observations.title: emart24 self-checkout
observations.place: Daejeon, emart24 Chungnam National University branch
observations.scenario: Scanning and paying for purchases without a cashier in a convenience store.

unverified: Which payment methods work with a foreign card

media.caption: Self-checkout screen with the printed step guide above it.

observed: A printed guide above the screen shows five steps: prepare, scan barcode, discount or points, pay (card or SSG PAY), done.
The guide adds two rules: scan every item in a 1+1 or 2+1 promotion, and ask staff to process alcohol and tobacco.
The screen repeats the same steps as tabs: 상품등록 (add items), 할인적립 (discounts and points), 결제수단 (payment method), 결제완료 (done).
Each item shows its own discount on a separate red line. Two jellies show −2,000 ₩, so the second one is free (1+1).
Totals: 8,300 ₩, discount −2,600 ₩, to pay 5,700 ₩.
Quick buttons at the bottom cover items without a barcode: shopping bags at 100 and 250 ₩, bottled water.
A 글자확대 (enlarge text) button sits in the bottom bar.
Separate buttons for partner discounts or points and for emart24's own quick payment.
An Apple Pay sticker on the frame. A handwritten yellow sticky note reads 가져가세요 (“please take it”).
interpretation: Discounts and loyalty points are a separate step placed between scanning and payment.
open: How common are 1+1 and 2+1 promotions in Korean convenience stores, and why? Needs a source.
When did Apple Pay launch in Korea? Check.
What does the 가져가세요 note refer to?

observations.title: Hanjin delivery notifications
observations.scenario: Receiving a parcel while not at home.

unverified: Can the drop-off and tracking page be used without a Korean phone number?

media.caption: Step 1. Text message: the courier is on the way.
Step 2. Text message: delivered, with a photo of the drop-off spot.

observed: Both messages come from an ordinary mobile number (+82 10-…), not a short service number.
The first message lists the item name, tracking number, sender, address and a delivery window of 14:00–16:00.
It links to a page for choosing a drop-off spot (위탁장소) and tracking the courier in real time.
It ends by asking the recipient to remove the label and packaging and sort them for recycling.
The second message says the parcel was left at the drop-off spot (문앞, “in front of the door”) because nobody was home, with the exact time 13:39:27.
A photo is attached. It shows a pile of many residents' parcels on the floor of a shared hallway, not a door.
interpretation: The photo works as proof of delivery.
In a dormitory, “in front of the door” in practice means a shared hallway.
open: Is the sender number the courier's personal phone or a masked relay number? Check.
Is the delivery photo a Hanjin standard or up to the courier?
observations.rights: Own screenshots. Phone number, tracking number, address, sender and parcel labels are blurred.

observations.subject: metaclub
observations.scenario: A student selects a dormitory washing machine, confirms laundry detergent instructions, and pays using in-app points before exploring student community features.

requires: Bluetooth and Location enabled on smartphone
Proximity to the washing machine during Bluetooth pairing and payment
unverified: Is university student email verification required to access campus-specific laundry rooms and community boards?

observed: A pop-up modal reminds users that washing machine timers display estimated completion times and instructs users to insert capsule detergent directly into the drum, never into the detergent tray.
The app requires Bluetooth and location services turned on to scan QR codes or connect to dorm washing machines.
Connecting to the machine can take up to 1 minute over Bluetooth.
Standard washer cycle costs 1,200P, deducted from MetaMoney points balance.
Before payment proceeds, a full-screen warning modal requires confirmation that the user is standing directly in front of the machine and will keep the screen active.
The app shows a list of CNU dorm buildings (생활관 7동, 11동, 12동, 10동, 8동, 13동, 9동) for selecting laundry rooms.
A dedicated usage history logs the exact machine, room location, timestamp, and status ('In Use', 'Completed') with a 'Try Again' button if the machine fails to start.
The app includes peripheral campus features: gift voucher purchases with discounts, student contest/extracurricular boards, team recruitment, and student profile/nickname setup.
interpretation: The strict proximity warning modal suggests payments commonly fail or trigger machine lockouts if users walk away before Bluetooth handshake completes.
Integrating laundry controls with gift card discounts and team project recruitment suggests the app acts as a broader university campus lifestyle platform.
open: What happens if payment succeeds in the app but the washing machine hardware fails to trigger a start signal?
Can non-residents or visitors use the washers if they download the app, or is resident dorm verification enforced?

observed: The library kiosk features a touchscreen displaying '열람실 좌석 이용 신청' (Reading room seat reservation) and instructions to scan a student ID or QR code to log in.

The kiosk hardware includes an RFID card reader, a QR and barcode scanner, an accessible tactile numeric keypad, a headphone jack, a volume knob, assistance call and magnification buttons, and a motorized height adjustment switch.
The library mobile app provides a dynamic 'Mobile Card' QR code with a 60-second countdown timer alongside student enrollment details and local weather.
Entrance posters instruct users to scan a QR code with a smartphone camera to issue a daily pass ('일일이용증 발급 및 출입 안내').
The mobile application mixes English ('Seat Reservation', 'Mobile Loan', 'Loan History') with Korean text ('디자인창의학과', '재학').
interpretation: The author interpreted the seat allocation request ('좌석 이용 신청') as purchasing tickets ('покупка билетов').
The partial English localization in the university app can cause confusion for international students despite selecting English as the interface language.
open: Does the seat reservation kiosk support a full English interface mode when toggling the on-screen language selector?
How long does an allocated seat reservation remain active before expiring if the student fails to swipe into the reading room gate?
